limitations: Paper full text unreadable: aacrjournals.org returned HTTP 403 for the PDF and HTML (no bypass attempted); not in PMC. The paper was found by Europe PMC title/author search (PMID 33446566). Its citation of PXD020618 could NOT be verified from the paper text; the link rests on PRIDE title = paper title, identical authors (Harel, Geiger), the PRIDE protocols, and the deposited MaxQuant experiment names matching Table S1A/S1B sample names 1:1 (186 experiments vs 185 S1A rows, PD49+PD58 merged).

Partial deposit: PXD020618 holds 338 RAW files = 70 of the 185 S1A samples (TIL45-86, TIL25, TIL33, PD3, PD22, PD34, PD42, PD48, PD58, CTLA1-18, CTLA20, CTLA21). The other ~115 samples searched in the same MaxQuant run (TIL1-44, most PD) are not in this deposit (TIL cohort and PD1 runs partly in PXD006003). All 338 deposited runs are annotated.

Deposited file names differ from acquisition names in the raw headers for 27 files (e.g. 20170322_MH_SA_TIL_84_* acquired as 20170322_MH_SA_PD1_35_*; TIL_75 and TIL_77 swapped; TIL_85/TIL_86 acquired as TIL_43/TIL_44; Animal_20180726_SA_MH_CTLA4_20 acquired as ..._CTLA4_21). Sample identity follows the deposited names, which are the names MaxQuant searched (summary.txt) and therefore the data the paper reports; CTLA4_20.raw was renamed after the search and is mapped to MaxQuant experiment CTLA20 via its acquisition path (raw header) = summary.txt raw "Animal_20180726_SA_MH_CTLA4_21".

Super-SILAC cell-line identities (WM266-4, WM115, A375, mel526, mel624) are stated in Harel et al. 2019, the protocol PRIDE cites; the PRIDE text for this deposit says only "five SILAC-labeled melanoma cell lines".

Sample-prep protocol per technical set inferred: set 1 (TIL25, TIL33; 2014) = Harel TIL-cohort FASP/trypsin/SAX; sets 2-3 = TFE/Lys-C+trypsin/SCX (PRIDE protocol, SCX method names). reconcile (v3 record) BLOCKER on the TIL25/TIL33 Lys-C "not applicable" is refuted on that basis in validation.txt.
Age = S1A "Age at treatment" floored to whole years; samples were taken shortly before treatment start (or up to 219 days after for 8 on-treatment samples), so age at sampling may differ by <1 year.
Treatment response is the response to the immunotherapy of the patient's group (S1A Response); the response criteria (RECIST/irRC) are not readable (paper inaccessible) -> generic NCIT terms.

TIL68/69/71/74/79 each have two 240-min single-shot runs that MaxQuant labelled fraction 1 and 2; annotated as technical replicates 1/2 of fraction 1 (same method, second has the Xcalibur re-acquisition timestamp), not as fractions.

Four deposited runs were never searched (in the MaxQuant design as CTLA3 / named TIL86, absent from summary.txt): tolerances and the search-only variable mods are "not applicable"; Carbamidomethyl C (both channels) and the Arg10/Lys8 labels (heavy rows) are kept as sample chemistry (coordinator decision, consistent with PXD024103/PXD004817). parse_sdrf convert-openms therefore fails ("Cannot read precursor mass tolerance: not applicable"); the 668 searched rows convert cleanly (probe in validation.txt).
techsdrf not installed: instrument, NCE, MS1 scan range read from HTTP-range reads (384 KB) of each raw header.
Precursor tolerance 4.5 ppm is the Andromeda main-search value (.apar); MaxQuant first-search tolerance (mqpar.xml) not deposited.

Therapy group (characteristics/factor value[treatment]) is fully confounded with technical set, sample-preparation batch and instrument/acquisition period (TIL25/33 2014 set 1; TIL45-86 2017 set 2; PD 2016-18; CTLA 2018 set 3 on QE Plus); the paper corrected batch with limma, the SDRF cannot.
Lys-C for the unfractionated single-shot runs of sets 2-3 (TIL68/69/71/74/79, CTLA20) is inferred from technical set only.
convert-openms: filter out the 8 rows of the 4 never-searched runs (tolerance not applicable) before conversion for quantms.

Survival: S1A gives one OS value plus Death; it is split into survival time (deceased) and last follow up (alive, censored). The OS origin (diagnosis vs treatment start) is not readable (paper inaccessible).

Eight annotated samples are flagged "Low proteomic quality" in S1A (TIL68, TIL69, TIL71, TIL74, TIL79, TIL25, TIL33, CTLA20) and were excluded from the paper analyses; kept and flagged in characteristics[clinical data].
